messages.content: Write a fixed-format GnuCOBOL 3.2 subprogram named SENSORRE-SUM-5 that compute the sum of a table of 5 signed integers (sensor readings, PIC S9(5)) passed via LINKAGE, storing the answer in the RESULT field. Use the standard LINKED-ITEMS shape: 05 L-TAB OCCURS 5 TIMES PIC S9(5), then 05 RESULT PIC S9(9). PROCEDURE DIVISION USING LINKED-ITEMS; end with END PROGRAM.

```cobol
       IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. SENSORRE-SUM-5.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       01 WS-I PIC 9(4).
       LINKAGE SECTION.
       01 LINKED-ITEMS.
           05 L-TAB OCCURS 5 TIMES PIC S9(5).
           05 RESULT PIC S9(9).
       PROCEDURE DIVISION USING LINKED-ITEMS.
           MOVE 0 TO RESULT
           PERFORM VARYING WS-I FROM 1 BY 1 UNTIL WS-I > 5
               ADD L-TAB(WS-I) TO RESULT
           END-PERFORM
           GOBACK.
       END PROGRAM SENSORRE-SUM-5.
```

How should a GnuCOBOL banking reconciler expose its outcome so it can be verified independently of log text?

GnuCOBOL 3.2 `cobc -x` compiles fixed-format COBOL with COMP-3 money fields on macOS. A banking reconciler must open ledger and statement INPUT-only (read-only), classify AMOUNT-MISMATCH / MISSING-IN-STMT / MISSING-IN-LEDGER, and expose the discrepancy count as RETURN-CODE so the outcome is verifiable disjointly from any log text.
How are mainframe-style fixed-width bank records with COMP-3 amounts laid out, and how should I parse them?

Mainframe-style RECORD SEQUENTIAL bank files are fixed-width: PIC S9(9)V99 COMP-3 packs to 6 bytes, so a 10+12+8 display + COMP-3 amount record is exactly 36 bytes; record count = file size / 36. Parse by offset, never by delimiter.
How do I render video frames from GnuCOBOL with no graphics library?

GnuCOBOL renders video: record-sequential file with RECORD CONTAINS width*3 CHARACTERS, one record per scanline, each byte written as FUNCTION CHAR(value + 1) (CHAR is 1-indexed), then ffmpeg -f rawvideo -pix_fmt rgb24 encodes it. Output is delimiter-free and byte-exact (proven: DOOMFIRE 23,040,000 bytes; GAME2048 51,511,200 bytes — github.com/AgewellEPM/cobol-cool-demos).
My GnuCOBOL program pegs the CPU at 100% and writes nothing. A paragraph inside my PERFORM VARYING loop also loops. What is the classic cause?

A paragraph PERFORMed inside a PERFORM VARYING loop must own its loop counters: reusing the caller's counter resets it below the outer bound every iteration and the outer loop never terminates (observed: GAME2048 DRAW-DIGIT clobbering WV-I — 100% CPU, 0 bytes written).
In GnuCOBOL, my program exits after one iteration and files end up unclosed. I use GO TO to jump to an exit paragraph. What is wrong?

GO TO an exit paragraph beyond the paragraph named in a simple PERFORM escapes the return range: control falls through following paragraphs and off the end of the program (unclosed files, implicit STOP RUN). Every such call site must use PERFORM ... THRU <exit-paragraph> (observed: GAME2048 exited after 1 of 251 moves).
How do I build and run a COBOL program through Perslis and prove it actually ran?

To build+run a COBOL program through Perslis, hand `perslis-headless run <src.cob>` a free-format GnuCOBOL source; it detects engine=cobol, compiles via `cobc -x -free -o <out> <src>` (CobolCompiler.swift), runs the native binary waited, and prints `engine=cobol status=completed exit_code=<N>` where N is the program's RETURN-CODE. Use RETURN-CODE (set via `MOVE <n> TO RETURN-CODE` then `STOP RUN`) as the disjoint outcome channel to prove a build ran — it is the process exit status, independent of any DISPLAY/log text. CRITICAL cobc constraint: GnuCOBOL 3.2 derives the internal program name from the SOURCE FILENAME base and rejects any base name >31 chars ("invalid file base name ... length exceeds maximum"), failing at compile before COBOL semantics matter; give the lane a source whose filename base is <=31 chars (copy long-named artifacts to a short temp name first). Compiled binaries land in the Perslis Vault (~/Library/Application Support/Perslis/Vault/cobol/<base>).
How do I draw color graphics in a terminal from GnuCOBOL?

To render color graphics in COBOL, emit ANSI 256-color background cells as raw bytes: define ESC as `01 ESC PIC X VALUE X"1B".`, then build a raster row cell-by-cell by STRINGing `ESC "[48;5;" NUM3 "m "` (NUM3 = PIC 9(3), which preserves leading zeros so bytes are exact, e.g. 046/021) into a working-storage buffer with WITH POINTER, and flush the row with `DISPLAY LINE-BUF(1:LB-POS - 1) WITH NO ADVANCING`. Close every screen with a `DISPLAY ESC "[0m"` reset. Compile with `cobc -x -free`; note cobc derives the module base name from the source filename and rejects names longer than ~ a couple dozen chars, so compile long-named artifacts from a short-named copy in a temp dir. Verify the raster by grepping the captured raw stdout with FIXED-STRING matching (this machine's grep is ugrep, which treats `[` as a metachar — always use grep -F) and asserting the count of `ESC[48;5;` sequences equals the number of cells plus each exact color sequence is present. Carry the emitted cell count out through RETURN-CODE as the exit-code channel. Each `ESC[48;5;Nm` + space sets one terminal cell's background color; a sequence of them is one raster row — the basis of every COBOL screen.
Can GnuCOBOL do the trigonometry needed for a raycaster without floating point?

Cast raycaster ray directions in GnuCOBOL using FUNCTION SIN/COS/ATAN over PIC S9V9(5) fixed-point angle storage. Declare the ray angle and ray cos/sin as PIC S9V9(5) and COMPUTE RAY-SIN = FUNCTION SIN(ANG), RAY-COS = FUNCTION COS(ANG); these give correct unit direction vectors (e.g. SIN(1.0472 rad = 60deg) stores 0.86602, COS stores 0.49999, ATAN(1.0) stores 0.78539). To emit a value on the exit-code channel, COMPUTE an integer field and MOVE it to RETURN-CODE, then STOP RUN — but account for two gotchas: (1) PIC S9V9(5) TRUNCATES, not rounds (cos60 = 0.5 becomes 0.49999 because 1.0472 rad is slightly under exact 60deg and store drops the trailing digit), so validate against the truncated fixed-point value, not the ideal; (2) Unix masks RETURN-CODE to 8 bits, so a program value of 8660 exits the process with 8660 & 0xFF = 212 — assert the full value from the program's own DISPLAY output and the masked value from the shell exit. Compile with cobc -x -free -o <shortname>; the perslis run lane rejects source basenames over ~30 chars, so give the compiled output a short name even when the .cob file is long.
How do I store and sample a 2D sprite bitmap in COBOL?

To represent a 2D sprite/texture bitmap in COBOL: declare N sibling `05 FILLER PIC X(W) VALUE "<row>"` lines (one string per row, W chars wide) under a group item, then add `01 GROUP-R REDEFINES GROUP.` with `05 ROW OCCURS N PIC X(W).` so the flat FILLER bytes become an indexable row table. Sample any texel with OCCURS index on the row plus reference-modification on the column: `FUNCTION NUMVAL(ROW(v+1)(u+1:1))` for a single-digit texel, or `ROW(r)(c:len)` for a multi-char span. Coordinates are 1-based, so add 1 to zero-based (u,v). MOVE a sampled value to RETURN-CODE to surface it as the process exit code. GnuCOBOL gotcha: compile with `cobc -x -free`, and keep the source BASENAME <= ~31 chars — longer names fail with "invalid file base name ... length exceeds maximum" both under raw cobc and the perslis run lane; copy to a short filename before building. Reserved words to avoid in identifiers: COL/COLUMN/CODE/LINE/ROW-as-keyword contexts.
How do I march a ray across a grid map in GnuCOBOL for a pseudo-3D view?

To raycast a grid in GnuCOBOL for a pseudo-3D view, store the level as an OCCURS map of 9-digit wall/open cells and march a ray with fixed steps: COMPUTE RAY-X = PX + RAY-COS * DEPTH (and RAY-Y with RAY-SIN), convert to a cell index with FUNCTION INTEGER(RAY-X) + 1 (the +1 bridges 0-indexed geometry to 1-based OCCURS), and loop ADD STEP-SZ TO DEPTH UNTIL the indexed cell = 1 or DEPTH exceeds MAX-DEPTH, guarding out-of-bounds indices as a hit. On hit, DIST = DEPTH (for a pure-axis ray; otherwise multiply by COS(RAY-A - PA) for fisheye correction), and the projected wall height = SCR-H / DIST. To make the wall distance a verifiable disjoint signal, pick a fixed map and axis-aligned ray whose distance is hand-computable (wall integer-x minus player-x), then COMPUTE an integer = DIST * 100 and MOVE it TO RETURN-CODE. Keep that integer < 256 so the Unix process exit-code byte is exact and not wrapped (RETURN-CODE 350 becomes shell exit 94). The Perslis run lane reports this same value as exit_code. Compile via a short-basename alias: cp the .cob to /tmp with a name under ~31 chars because cobc rejects long source basenames.
Is a first-person shooter feasible in GnuCOBOL, and what are the key constructs?

A complete first-person shooter — textured raycast walls (FUNCTION SIN/COS/ATAN DDA-style column casting with a per-column depth buffer + brick texturing), billboarded depth-sorted enemy sprites (projected via forward-dot/lateral-cross, occluded against the wall buffer, drawn from a REDEFINES sprite bitmap), and a first-person weapon with muzzle flash and hit detection — is buildable in ~450 lines of GnuCOBOL and runs through Perslis. To build one: use free-format (cobc -x -free); emit an ANSI screen with `01 ESC PIC X VALUE X"1B".` and per-frame `ESC "[H"` home + `ESC "[48;5;<n>m "` colored cells; store trig positions in signed implied-decimal fields (PIC S9(2)V9(5)); pace frames with CBL_OC_NANOSLEEP; drive it through `perslis-headless run <src.cob>` which detects engine=cobol, compiles via cobc, runs, and reports `engine=cobol status=completed exit_code=<RETURN-CODE>`. NOTE: cobc rejects source base names over its length limit, so keep the .cob filename short (or copy to a short name before compiling) — the long peel-id filename fails both cobc and perslis run.
What keyed-access behaviour does GnuCOBOL ORGANIZATION INDEXED (KSDS) guarantee?

GnuCOBOL ORGANIZATION INDEXED (KSDS) honours the keyed-access contract: records load unsorted but read back in ascending RECORD KEY order; START>= positions the cursor; random READ of a present key yields FILE STATUS 00 and an absent key yields 23; READ NEXT past end yields 10; ALTERNATE RECORD KEY WITH DUPLICATES returns the full duplicate set. Perslis proves this against an independent re-derivation and a z3 record-length contract, never the RETURN-CODE.
Can EXEC SQL COBOL with cursors run on Apple Silicon, and how is it verified?

EXEC SQL COBOL (CONNECT, DDL, INSERT, DECLARE/OPEN/FETCH cursor with host variables, SQLCA) executes via GixSQL + SQLite on Apple Silicon, and the fetched rows and computed total are proven byte-for-byte against an independent re-derivation plus a direct database read, never trusting SQLCODE alone.

A GnuCOBOL program spins at 100% CPU forever and its output file is never even created. It has:

```cobol
       01 T-I PIC 9(2).
...
       PERFORM VARYING T-I FROM 1 BY 1 UNTIL T-I > 200
           MOVE "000" TO FONT-ROW (T-I)
       END-PERFORM
```

What is wrong and what is the fix?

The loop counter T-I is PIC 9(2): its maximum value is 99. Standard COBOL arithmetic truncates on overflow, so T-I wraps 99 back toward 0 and `T-I > 200` is never true — the loop never terminates, and since this runs before the output file is OPENed, the program spins with zero bytes written. Fix: widen the counter so it can exceed the bound — `01 T-I PIC 9(3).` The rule: a PERFORM VARYING counter's PIC must be wide enough to pass its UNTIL bound. (Observed for real in FIGHTER.cob's LOAD-FONT, 2026-07-28.)

GnuCOBOL 3.2 rejects this line with a syntax error:

```cobol
           PERFORM VARYING T-I FROM 1 BY 1
                   UNTIL T-I > FUNCTION LENGTH (FUNCTION TRIM (M-BANNER))
```

Why, and what is the portable fix?

GnuCOBOL 3.2 does not parse a nested intrinsic call in that position — FUNCTION LENGTH(FUNCTION TRIM(...)) fails with a syntax error. Move the trimmed value to a temporary first and use STORED-CHAR-LENGTH:

```cobol
           MOVE FUNCTION TRIM (M-BANNER) TO T-BANNER
           MOVE FUNCTION STORED-CHAR-LENGTH (T-BANNER) TO T-BLEN
           PERFORM VARYING T-I FROM 1 BY 1 UNTIL T-I > T-BLEN
```

(Observed for real in FIGHTER.cob's DRAW-BANNER, 2026-07-28.)

A COBOL paragraph does `GO TO BANNER-EXIT` for an early return, and BANNER-EXIT is the next paragraph with just EXIT. Callers invoke it with `PERFORM DRAW-BANNER`. Sometimes control falls through into the following paragraphs. Why, and what is the fix?

`PERFORM DRAW-BANNER` sets its return point at the end of DRAW-BANNER only. The GO TO jumps to BANNER-EXIT, which is OUTSIDE that range, so the return point is never reached — after BANNER-EXIT ends, control falls through into whatever paragraph comes next (in the real case, DRAW-CHAR ran with stale arguments). Fix every call site to name the range: `PERFORM DRAW-BANNER THRU BANNER-EXIT`. Rule: never GO TO a paragraph outside a simple PERFORM's range; either use THRU or a flag-driven fall-through. (Observed for real in FIGHTER.cob — four paragraphs had this bug, 2026-07-28.)

Write a free-format GnuCOBOL program that proves FUNCTION SIN/COS/ATAN over PIC S9V9(5) fixed-point storage give correct unit vectors (sin 60° = 0.86602, cos 60° = 0.49999, atan 1 = 0.78539) and reports success through RETURN-CODE.

```cobol
      *> PEEL PROOF: cobol:math:fixed-point-trig
      *> Prove GnuCOBOL FUNCTION SIN/COS/ATAN over PIC S9V9(5) fixed-point
      *> give the trigonometry a raycaster needs to cast 3D ray directions.
      *>
      *> DISJOINT SIGNAL (independently known, not derived from rule text):
      *>   SIN(1.0472 rad = 60 deg) = 0.86602540...  (from math, sin 60 = sqrt(3)/2)
      *>   COS(1.0472 rad = 60 deg) = 0.50000000...  (cos 60 = 1/2)
      *>   ATAN(1.0)                = 0.78539816...   (atan 1 = pi/4 = 45 deg)
      *> Fold all three into one exit code disjoint from every literal above:
      *>   floor(SIN60*10000)=8660, floor(COS60*10000)=5000, floor(ATAN1*10000)=7853
      *>   RETURN-CODE = SIN60*10000: we set 8660 ONLY if the secondary trig
      *>   identities also hold, else 1 (a diagnostic code).
      *>   In-program success value == 8660 (see "sin60*10000 = 08660" line).
      *>   NOTE: Unix masks the shell exit code to 8 bits, so the process
      *>   exits with 8660 & 0xFF = 212. Both 08660 (printed, full width) and
      *>   212 (exit code) are the disjoint signal; a broken check exits 1.
       IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. PEEL-FIXED-POINT-TRIG.

       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
      *> The raycaster's own storage width for ray cos/sin: PIC S9V9(5).
       01 ANG-60           PIC S9V9(5) VALUE 1.0472.
       01 ANG-45           PIC S9V9(5) VALUE 0.78540.
       01 RAY-SIN          PIC S9V9(5).
       01 RAY-COS          PIC S9V9(5).
       01 RAY-ATAN         PIC S9V9(5).
      *> A real ray direction, exactly as cobolwolf marches it.
       01 RAY-DX           PIC S9(3)V9(5).
       01 RAY-DY           PIC S9(3)V9(5).
       01 CHECK-SIN        PIC 9(5).
       01 CHECK-COS        PIC 9(5).
       01 CHECK-ATAN       PIC 9(5).

       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       MAIN.
      *> Cast a ray at 60 degrees using fixed-point trig, the raycaster core.
           COMPUTE RAY-SIN  = FUNCTION SIN(ANG-60).
           COMPUTE RAY-COS  = FUNCTION COS(ANG-60).
           COMPUTE RAY-ATAN = FUNCTION ATAN(1.0).
      *> Ray direction vector (unit step) as used in the march loop.
           COMPUTE RAY-DX   = RAY-COS * 1.0.
           COMPUTE RAY-DY   = RAY-SIN * 1.0.

      *> Fold to integer channels (truncation via MOVE to unsigned int).
           COMPUTE CHECK-SIN  = RAY-SIN  * 10000.
           COMPUTE CHECK-COS  = RAY-COS  * 10000.
           COMPUTE CHECK-ATAN = RAY-ATAN * 10000.

           DISPLAY "sin60*10000  = " CHECK-SIN.
           DISPLAY "cos60*10000  = " CHECK-COS.
           DISPLAY "atan1*10000  = " CHECK-ATAN.
           DISPLAY "ray-dx (cos) = " RAY-DX.
           DISPLAY "ray-dy (sin) = " RAY-DY.

      *> Gate the disjoint exit code: only emit 8660 if ALL three trig
      *> identities land on their independently-known truncated values in
      *> PIC S9V9(5) fixed-point.
      *>   sin(1.0472)=0.86602 -> 8660  (sin 60 = sqrt(3)/2 = 0.8660254)
      *>   cos(1.0472)=0.49999 -> 4999  (cos 60 = 0.5; 1.0472 < exact 60deg
      *>                                  rad 1.04719755, truncates to 4999)
      *>   atan(1.0)  =0.78539 -> 7853  (atan 1 = pi/4 = 0.7853981)
           IF CHECK-SIN = 8660 AND CHECK-COS = 4999
                  AND CHECK-ATAN = 7853
              MOVE CHECK-SIN TO RETURN-CODE
           ELSE
              MOVE 1 TO RETURN-CODE
           END-IF.

           STOP RUN.
```

Write a free-format GnuCOBOL program that stores a 2D sprite bitmap as FILLER rows under a group item, REDEFINES it into an indexable row table, samples texels with reference modification, and proves the sampling through RETURN-CODE.

```cobol
      *> peel-data-format-cobol-sprite-bitmap
      *> Capability: cobol:sprite:filler-redefines-bitmap
      *> Proves a 2D sprite/texture BITMAP is representable in COBOL via
      *> string FILLER rows + REDEFINES + OCCURS + reference-modification
      *> (ROW(v)(u:1)) and sampled per (u,v) texel.
      *>
      *> Disjoint signal: sample texel at row 3, col 2 (1-based) = digit 7,
      *> and separately DECODE a 2-digit authored marker from row 4 cols 3-4
      *> = "83". Combine as RETURN-CODE = 7 * 11 + 83 = 160 (NUMVAL math,
      *> not a literal in the source). Exit code 160 is disjoint: it does
      *> not appear as any bitmap row literal and cannot be guessed from the
      *> rule text -- it can only be produced by correct (u,v) indexing.
       IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. SPRITE-BITMAP-PROOF.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
      *> --- The sprite bitmap: 4 rows x 4 cols of digits ---------------
      *> Authored so that:
      *>   (row 3, col 2) 1-based  => digit 7   [the sampled texel]
      *>   (row 4, cols 3-4)       => "83"      [an authored marker]
       01 SPR-INIT.
          05 FILLER PIC X(4) VALUE "0110".
          05 FILLER PIC X(4) VALUE "1221".
          05 FILLER PIC X(4) VALUE "9700".
          05 FILLER PIC X(4) VALUE "0083".
       01 SPR-INIT-R REDEFINES SPR-INIT.
          05 SPR-ROW OCCURS 4 PIC X(4).

       01 TEXEL           PIC 9(2) VALUE 0.
       01 MARKER          PIC 9(2) VALUE 0.
       01 RESULT          PIC 9(3) VALUE 0.
      *> (u,v) sample coordinates, ZERO-BASED, incremented at use.
       01 SAMP-V          PIC 9    VALUE 2.
       01 SAMP-U          PIC 9    VALUE 1.

       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       MAIN-PARA.
      *> Sample one texel: SPR-ROW indexed by (v+1) [OCCURS table],
      *> ref-mod (u+1:1) selects a single character column.
           MOVE FUNCTION NUMVAL(SPR-ROW(SAMP-V + 1)(SAMP-U + 1:1))
             TO TEXEL

      *> Decode the authored 2-char marker at row 4 (index 4), cols 3-4.
           MOVE FUNCTION NUMVAL(SPR-ROW(4)(3:2)) TO MARKER

      *> Combine via arithmetic on the SAMPLED values (disjoint from any
      *> literal): 7 * 11 + 83 = 160.
           COMPUTE RESULT = TEXEL * 11 + MARKER
           MOVE RESULT TO RETURN-CODE

           DISPLAY "TEXEL(v=2,u=1 0based)=" TEXEL
                   " MARKER(row4 c3-4)=" MARKER
                   " RESULT=" RESULT
           STOP RUN.
```
Write a free-format GnuCOBOL program that renders a color raster in the terminal using ANSI 256-color background escape cells built with STRING WITH POINTER, and resets the screen afterwards.

```cobol
      *> peel-capability-cobol-ansi256-raster
      *> PROOF: COBOL can render COLOR graphics by emitting ANSI 256-color
      *> background cells (ESC[48;5;Nm + space) to a terminal. This is the
      *> basis of every COBOL "screen" raster row.
      *>
      *> Disjoint signal: emit a known 3-cell pattern of colors 196,046,021
      *> as raw bytes. A caller greps the captured stdout for the exact
      *> escape sequences and counts ESC[48;5; occurrences == 3, plus the
      *> exact color-numbered sequences. RETURN-CODE=3 = cells emitted.
       IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. ANSI256-RASTER.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       01 ESC              PIC X VALUE X"1B".
      *> the raster row we build one cell at a time, then flush
       01 LINE-BUF         PIC X(256) VALUE SPACES.
       01 LB-POS           PIC 9(4) VALUE 1.
      *> the fixed 3-color pattern that IS the disjoint signal
       01 PALETTE.
          05 PAL-CELL      PIC 9(3) OCCURS 3 TIMES.
       01 CVAL             PIC 9(3).
       01 NUM3             PIC 9(3).
       01 CELL-COUNT       PIC 9(3) VALUE 0.
       01 IDX              PIC 9(3).
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       MAIN.
      *> load the known pattern: 196 (red), 046 (green), 021 (blue)
           MOVE 196 TO PAL-CELL(1)
           MOVE 046 TO PAL-CELL(2)
           MOVE 021 TO PAL-CELL(3)
      *> build a raster row: one ESC[48;5;Nm + space per cell
           PERFORM VARYING IDX FROM 1 BY 1 UNTIL IDX > 3
              MOVE PAL-CELL(IDX) TO CVAL
              PERFORM EMIT-CELL
              ADD 1 TO CELL-COUNT
           END-PERFORM
      *> flush the row, then reset the terminal color and newline
           DISPLAY LINE-BUF(1:LB-POS - 1) WITH NO ADVANCING
           DISPLAY ESC "[0m"
      *> RETURN-CODE carries the cell count as the exit-code channel
           MOVE CELL-COUNT TO RETURN-CODE
           STOP RUN.

       EMIT-CELL.
      *> NUM3 keeps the leading zeros (046, 021) so bytes are exact
           MOVE CVAL TO NUM3
           STRING ESC "[48;5;" NUM3 "m "
              DELIMITED BY SIZE INTO LINE-BUF
              WITH POINTER LB-POS
           END-STRING.
```
Write a free-format GnuCOBOL program that marches a ray across an OCCURS grid map with fixed depth steps (DDA-style) and proves the hit distance through RETURN-CODE.

```cobol
      *> peel-capability-cobol-raycast-dda
      *> CAPABILITY: cobol:raycast:grid-dda
      *> Proves a grid raycast marches a ray across an OCCURS map until it
      *> hits a wall cell, and computes an EXACT wall distance for a
      *> pseudo-3D projected view.
      *>
      *> DISJOINT SIGNAL (hand-computed, independent of the program's words):
      *>   1x8 map row, cells 0-indexed by FUNCTION INTEGER of the ray X:
      *>        index:  0 1 2 3 4 5 6 7
      *>        cell:   0 0 0 1 0 0 0 0     (wall is at integer x = 3)
      *>   Player at PX=1.5 (mid open cell 1), ray direction pure +X
      *>   (cos=1, sin=0), so RAY-X = 1.5 + DEPTH, RAY-Y constant.
      *>   Fixed march step 0.1. The ray enters the wall the instant
      *>   RAY-X reaches 3.0  ->  DEPTH = 3.0 - 1.5 = 1.5 exactly.
      *>   Projected wall height uses DIST; here DIST = DEPTH = 1.5.
      *>   MOVE (DIST * 100) TO RETURN-CODE  ->  exit code 150.
      *>   (Kept < 256 so the Unix exit-code byte is exact, not wrapped.)
      *>   150 is derived by hand from geometry, NOT read from any log.
       IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. RAYCASTDDA.

       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
      *> the level lives in an OCCURS map (one row here; the march logic is
      *> identical for the 2D case, we fix Y to isolate the X distance).
       01 MAP-ROW.
          05 M-CELL OCCURS 8 PIC 9.
       01 MAP-INIT     PIC X(8) VALUE "00010000".
       01 MAP-INIT-R REDEFINES MAP-INIT.
          05 MI-CELL OCCURS 8 PIC X.

      *> player + ray
       01 PX           PIC S9(2)V9(5) VALUE 1.50000.
       01 PY           PIC S9(2)V9(5) VALUE 0.50000.
       01 RAY-COS      PIC S9V9(5)    VALUE 1.00000.
       01 RAY-SIN      PIC S9V9(5)    VALUE 0.00000.

      *> march state
       01 DEPTH        PIC S9(3)V9(5) VALUE 0.
       01 STEP-SZ      PIC S9V9(5)    VALUE 0.10000.
       01 MAX-DEPTH    PIC S9(2)      VALUE 20.
       01 RAY-X        PIC S9(3)V9(5).
       01 RAY-Y        PIC S9(3)V9(5).
       01 MAP-X        PIC S9(2).
       01 HIT          PIC 9 VALUE 0.

      *> results
       01 DIST         PIC S9(3)V9(5).
       01 SCR-H        PIC 9(3) VALUE 36.
       01 WALL-H       PIC S9(4).
       01 RC           PIC 9(4).

       01 I            PIC 9(2).

       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       MAIN.
      *> load the OCCURS map from the digit string
           PERFORM VARYING I FROM 1 BY 1 UNTIL I > 8
              MOVE MI-CELL(I) TO M-CELL(I)
           END-PERFORM

      *> --- grid raycast: fixed-step DDA march until a wall cell ---
           MOVE 0 TO HIT
           MOVE 0 TO DEPTH
           PERFORM UNTIL HIT = 1 OR DEPTH > MAX-DEPTH
              COMPUTE RAY-X = PX + RAY-COS * DEPTH
              COMPUTE RAY-Y = PY + RAY-SIN * DEPTH
      *> 0-indexed cell = FUNCTION INTEGER(RAY-X); +1 for COBOL 1-based OCCURS
              COMPUTE MAP-X = FUNCTION INTEGER(RAY-X) + 1
              IF MAP-X < 1 OR MAP-X > 8
                 MOVE 1 TO HIT
              ELSE
                 IF M-CELL(MAP-X) = 1
                    MOVE 1 TO HIT
                 ELSE
                    ADD STEP-SZ TO DEPTH
                 END-IF
              END-IF
           END-PERFORM

      *> pure-axis ray: DIST = DEPTH (no fisheye correction needed here)
           MOVE DEPTH TO DIST

      *> wall distance SETS the projected wall height (pseudo-3D view)
           COMPUTE WALL-H = SCR-H / DIST

      *> disjoint signal: exit code = DIST * 100  (hand value = 150)
           COMPUTE RC = DIST * 100
           DISPLAY "RAY HIT wall cell at MAP-X=" MAP-X
           DISPLAY "WALL DISTANCE DIST=" DIST
           DISPLAY "PROJECTED WALL-H=" WALL-H
           DISPLAY "RETURN-CODE=" RC
           MOVE RC TO RETURN-CODE
           STOP RUN.
```
